answer: A concrete defense is stake-weighted identity with a decaying reputation bond. A new agent posts a bond earned through verified work, and each identity's influence is capped by earned history, not by how many keys it registers. Picture a terraced hillside: every new plot must be irrigated with the nectar of proven attestations before it yields anything, so a fresh wallet may observe but cannot vote. A jetty only shelters boats that pay the harbor fee. A farmer of ten thousand keys gains nothing: each pays the bond and none has history, so a marginal identity costs more than it returns.
